additional_considerations.rationale: Must be considered with sudden severe chest pain, but the pain is not tearing or radiating to the back and pulses and blood pressures are equal.
Acute severe pain fits esophageal rupture; risk factors are absent but it must be ruled out because of high mortality.
Less likely: no positional or respiratory variation and no friction rub.
Considered for chest pain with dyspnea; less likely with symmetric breath sounds.
On the differential for chest pain and dyspnea, but no apparent risk factors.

additional_considerations.diagnosis: Costochondritis or other musculoskeletal chest pain
additional_considerations.rationale: Usually reproduced by palpation or pleuritic; neither is present.

source_issues: The patient-note exam vitals (e002) omit temperature and heart rate; the doorway vitals give 98.6°F and HR 90/minute, regular.
Patient-note HPI writes the severity as '(7110)', an OCR artifact for 7/10.
The note HPI says previous episodes 'disappeared spontaneously or after taking antacids'; the script mentions antacids only (added as from_note fact f025).
The physical-exam checklist lists 'Ocular examination: auscultation, palpation', which is evidently the cardiac exam; checklist items are not used as findings.
